_about: Machine-readable assumptions registry seeded by A0 (de-risk spike). A8's preflight asserts env-support (halt loud + specific on unsupported), and the contract-guard validates Anthropic-side responses + creds shape at runtime (alarm + graceful-pause on drift). Decisions #29/#30/#31. Each entry: id, what, expected_contract, check (how to verify), supported_envs, implement_hint (what to build to support a new env), surface (preflight|contract|both). Optional: unverified_envs, the envs in supported_envs where the assumption is CLAIMED but has never been confirmed working there (with unverified_note saying what is missing). Preflight still runs the check on such an env, and adds one warning row naming every unverified assumption for the platform, so the claim is never mistaken for a confirmed one (docs/design-conventions.md: support claims rest on what has been confirmed).

assumptions.what: Host platform is one we have validated.
assumptions.expected_contract: $^O in {MSWin32, cygwin, msys} on a Windows host; darwin on a macOS host; linux inside the sandbox container.
assumptions.check: perl $^O / uname; membership test against supported_envs.
assumptions.implement_hint: Add a platform-support module entry (paths, shell, exec quoting, keep-awake API) for the new OS; until then preflight must halt loud naming the OS.

assumptions.what: The orchestrator + token-keeper HTTPS transport (usage GET + token-refresh POST), trusting the system cert store.
assumptions.expected_contract: curl present; on win32 a Schannel build (no CA file needed); on the Linux sandbox an OpenSSL build using /etc/ssl/certs; on macOS the system /usr/bin/curl (SecureTransport, system trust store); HTTPS GET to api.anthropic.com succeeds. The perl code shells out to curl (bp-http.pl) because the sandbox perl has no IO::Socket::SSL.
assumptions.check: curl --version (look for Schannel on win32); a probe HTTPS request returns a TLS-valid response.
assumptions.implement_hint: Ensure curl is installed for the platform (it is the HTTPS transport — there is no perl-SSL fallback).

assumptions.what: Perl with JSON for the orchestrator/guard (HTTPS is curl's job, not perl's).
assumptions.expected_contract: perl >=5.14 with JSON::PP loadable. IO::Socket::SSL / Net::SSLeay are NOT required and are absent from the sandbox image (verified in localhost/claude-sandbox:2.1.170) — the HTTP transport is curl (see bin.curl), so requiring perl-SSL here would falsely fail the supported sandbox.
assumptions.implement_hint: Install perl + JSON::PP (core since 5.14). HTTPS comes from curl; no perl SSL modules are needed.

assumptions.what: jq for hook JSON parsing (hooks fail-closed without it).
assumptions.expected_contract: jq present where butler hooks run (the sandbox).
assumptions.implement_hint: Install jq in the sandbox image; host hooks do not run by default.

assumptions.what: A system CA store the curl transport can validate against (Linux); on win32 curl is Schannel and uses the Windows store.
assumptions.expected_contract: A CA file path exists; on the Linux sandbox /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt; on host /usr/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt (cygwin); on macOS /etc/ssl/cert.pem (shipped with the OS).
assumptions.check: stat the candidate CA paths; assert at least one exists.
assumptions.implement_hint: Ensure the platform CA store curl uses is present (Linux: ca-certificates; win32: Schannel needs none).

assumptions.expected_contract: $BP_CREDS_PATH, else ~/.claude/.credentials.json exists and is readable; mode 0600 (sandbox) / 0644 (cygwin-cosmetic on host). On macOS, with no such file, the login Keychain generic password 'Claude Code-credentials' holds the same JSON (read with `security find-generic-password -s ... -w`; never written, never copied to a file). One lookup for every reader: plugins/butler/scripts/BpCreds.pm.
assumptions.check: stat + parse (file), or one bounded `security` read (macOS Keychain).
assumptions.implement_hint: Teach BpCreds.pm where the new platform keeps Claude Code's grant; every reader (usage gate, preflight, drive-solo token recovery, sitrep/spend) goes through it.

assumptions.expected_contract: claudeAiOauth.{accessToken:str, refreshToken:str, expiresAt:int(epoch ms), scopes:[str], subscriptionType:str, rateLimitTier:str}
assumptions.check: parse + assert keys/types; expiresAt is epoch-ms (> 1e12).
assumptions.implement_hint: If Anthropic renames fields, update the contract + the write-back mapping; alarm on drift.

assumptions.expected_contract: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with Bearer + 'anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20' + 'User-Agent: claude-code/<ver>' returns 200 with five_hour.{utilization:int 0-100, resets_at:ISO-8601} and seven_day.{...}.
assumptions.check: one probe GET at launch; validate field presence/types; unauth returns 429 (not an auth signal).
assumptions.unverified_note: No live usage GET has been confirmed from a Mac. The endpoint contract is platform-independent; the macOS path to it (Keychain credentials, system curl) is not.
assumptions.implement_hint: If the shape changes (renamed/missing field, non-200), the contract-guard alarms + graceful-pauses; pin the new shape here.

assumptions.expected_contract: POST https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token (Content-Type: application/json) body {grant_type:'refresh_token', refresh_token, client_id, scope} -> 200 {access_token, expires_in[, refresh_token]}. Premature refresh is rate-limited (429) by design.
assumptions.check: shape verified from Claude Code's own bundle; atomic write-back proven against a fixture; A8 ACTIVELY verifies one real in-band refresh near expiry and asserts 200 + contract.
assumptions.implement_hint: If the endpoint/domain/grant changes, alarm + pause; never assume success. Treat 429 as expected (backoff, in-band only).
assumptions.status: mechanism-proven; live-200 from our code not yet observed (blocked by premature-refresh 429); verified indirectly (Claude Code rotated the token).

assumptions.what: Public Claude Code OAuth client id.
assumptions.check: env override else the pinned default.
assumptions.implement_hint: If Anthropic rotates the public client id, update here; a 4xx invalid_client on refresh signals drift.

assumptions.what: Plugin PreToolUse hooks fire for a worker SUBAGENT's tool calls (containment + A4 gate depend on it).
assumptions.expected_contract: A settings/plugin PreToolUse hook fires on a subagent Edit/Write and can deny it; hook input carries agent_id/agent_type.
assumptions.check: SELF-TEST at preflight: dispatch a throwaway worker that attempts an out-of-scope edit; assert it is DENIED. Fail loud if containment is silently not firing.
assumptions.unverified_note: The subagent-hook self-test has never been run on a Mac.
assumptions.implement_hint: If a Claude Code version stops firing plugin hooks for subagents, containment is broken — halt loud; do not run a fleet.
assumptions.status: confirmed via docs + structural evidence; runtime self-assert is the durable proof (Decision #31).

assumptions.what: A long-blocking background command's completion re-invokes the (idle) interactive session.
assumptions.expected_contract: A detached command, on exit, delivers a notification that re-invokes the session (reporter auto-announce).
assumptions.check: PROVEN empirically (Probe 4). Robust fallback: bounded ~9-min long-poll + re-arm regardless.
assumptions.unverified_note: Probe 4 (a background command's completion re-invokes the session) was proven in the A0 environment (Windows host, Linux sandbox); it has never been run on a Mac.
assumptions.implement_hint: If re-invocation behavior changes, the bounded long-poll + re-arm still works; surface a warning.

assumptions.what: Container runtime for the sandbox surface.
assumptions.expected_contract: podman (or docker) present; sandbox image tag matches the Claude Code CLI version.
assumptions.implement_hint: Detect docker vs podman (already done elsewhere); on a host without either, dispatch-fleet is unsupported — halt loud.

assumptions.what: the sandbox has its OWN usable claudeAiOauth (independent /login grant, not a host copy)
assumptions.implement_hint: run `claude-sandbox` and `/login` once inside the sandbox; the grant persists (claude-home RW bind) and the keeper refreshes it, so fleets ride it

assumptions.what: The project root is a usable git repository — butler's ledgers, checkpoints and commits all assume git works.
assumptions.expected_contract: git -C <project root> resolves a git dir AND a trivial read succeeds. A .git FILE whose gitdir: target does not exist (the worktree-across-a-container-boundary shape) must be treated as unusable.
assumptions.check: Resolve the project root (BP_PROJECT_ROOT, else git rev-parse --show-toplevel, else cwd); run git rev-parse --git-dir and a trivial read; BP_ALLOW_NO_GIT=1 downgrades a failure to a visible warning.
assumptions.implement_hint: Provide git on PATH and a real repository at the project root; if git is deliberately unavailable, set BP_ALLOW_NO_GIT=1 to accept a degraded, checkpoint-less run.

assumptions.what: Worker jails (bp-jail.pl) get real /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/random and /dev/urandom device nodes, copied from the image's /opt/bp-jail-skel/dev.
assumptions.expected_contract: /opt/bp-jail-skel/dev/{null,zero,random,urandom} are character devices and no .no-device-nodes marker is present. A rootless image build cannot create device nodes: the Containerfile then leaves the marker, and bp-jail.pl falls back to empty regular files, which a worker redirecting to /dev/null or reading /dev/urandom misbehaves against.
assumptions.check: Are the skeleton's nodes character devices, and is the marker absent? A degraded skeleton is a WARNING, never a failure (BpJailDevices.pm, shared with bp-jail.pl).
assumptions.implement_hint: Build the sandbox image rootful (device nodes need mknod outside a user namespace); until then jailed workers get empty-file stand-ins, and bp-jail.pl warns when it creates a jail.
